mentl/7db2919:
A sequence's element byte-stride rides the high bits of its existing tag word
(the word holds sc*16 + tag, so the tag is word & 0xF and sc is word / 16, exact
since tag < 16 — no shift op). Zero-biased (decode_stride/stride_class): a
stride-4 word list writes sc 0, so pack_tag(0, 0) == 0 and every current list is
byte-identical; only a byte (sc 1) or packed float (sc 2/3) writes a nonzero
code. The flat leaf reads the stride live via load_strided (load_i8 for a packed
byte, load_i32 for a word), so a generic body reading a packed sequence never
assumes stride 4 — the substrate that makes String=[byte] sound without the
corruption the naive type merge caused.

alloc/list_set/index/push/concat/slice/drop_last/flat_fill all thread the
carried stride; snoc/concat/slice nodes carry the parent's sc, self-describing.
decode_stride (runtime, sc -> stride) lives in lists.mn beside its readers
because the micro RTLIBS blob has no src/; stride_class (emit, stride -> sc)
stays in types.mn.

clob/7dc3aab:
A QAT-trained .dense artifact's learned object is its effective-ternary
projection, not its latents, but eval-dense and regime --dense defaulted
to the latent view when neither --ternary nor an override was passed. That
silently reported a QAT core's meaningless latent NLL (~6.7 on the
diagnostic), which reads as a training failure rather than a wrong-view
mistake. Every QAT evaluation had to remember --ternary or be wrong.

Record the training mode in TrainedDense (serde default, so existing
artifacts load as Latent, which is correct for them) and resolve the view
from it: with neither flag, use the stamped deployment view (QAT ->
ternary, Latent -> latent). Keep --ternary as an explicit override and add
--latent for the reverse; the two are mutually exclusive. The resolved
view is printed to stderr so eval-dense's JSON on stdout stays clean.
perennials/7d97d47:
down() and move() both ignore non-primary pointers; up() did not. A
client leaning in and steadying the phone put a thumb on the sheet, and
its pointerup committed the half-drawn bed she was still drawing, then
deadened the rest of the stroke because the gesture was already gone.
It takes two fingers on a phone held out for someone else to see, which
is the posture this whole editor is for.

Cancel gets its own handler while I am here. It was wired to up(),
which committed whatever half of the stroke had arrived; the system
taking a gesture away is not the same as a finger finishing it, so it
throws the stroke out instead.
